question: "Constitutional morality acts as both a restraint and an enabler in a democratic society". Critically examine this statement in the context of recent judicial interpretations in India. (150 words)
candidate_answer:
Constitutional morality means morality is very good and people should follow moral values like helping others and respecting elders. If people have good morals and ethics then democracy will work fine without any fight.

Courts also say that government and citizens must be moral in daily life. But sometimes police and politicians don't follow morals so corruption happens. Therefore morality is needed in society so everyone can live peacefully together.

question: Discuss the relevance and challenges of holding simultaneous elections in India. Would it strengthen federalism or undermine it? (150 words)
candidate_answer:
Simultaneous elections are good because all elections will happen together on single day. Money will be saved which can be used for building roads and schools.

However opposition parties don't like it because EVMs can be hacked and national leaders will get all the votes. So it is very difficult to do in big country like India.

question: The role of tribunals in India has expanded but concerns about their independence and effectiveness persist. Critically evaluate the current tribunal system in light of recent judicial and legislative developments. (150 words)
candidate_answer:
Tribunals were created by Article 500 of the Indian Constitution by Lord Ripon. They are like High Courts and Supreme Court.

Chairman is directly appointed by Prime Minister without any exam. Tribunals decide cases very fast because judges are retired people with full knowledge. But government does not give enough building and computers to tribunals so pendency is increasing.

question: In light of increasing defections and political instability, do you think the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution needs a relook? Suggest reforms for strengthening anti-defection law. (150 words)
candidate_answer:
MLAs and MPs change party because other party gives them 50 crore rupees and hotel resort stay in Guwahati or Mumbai. This is called horse trading and it destroys democracy.

Anti defection law was brought by Rajiv Gandhi in 1985. The reform needed is that any politician who defects should be permanently jailed and not allowed to contest election for whole life.

question: "The success of good governance lies in citizen-centric administration." Examine the significance of the Sevottam model in this context. (150 words)
candidate_answer:
India has achieved historic success in space technology and planetary exploration. Recently ISRO successfully launched the Chandrayaan-3 lunar mission from Sriharikota, making India the first nation to land on the south pole of the Moon.

The Pragyan rover performed chemical experiments on the lunar surface and detected sulphur and oxygen. Furthermore, the Aditya-L1 solar observatory mission was sent to the Lagrange L1 point to study coronal mass ejections and space weather.

These remarkable scientific achievements have placed India at the top tier of space exploration under the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat.

question: How do Self-Help Groups (SHGs) contribute to participatory governance in India? (150 words)
candidate_answer:
SHG is Self Help Group. In villages poor women gather together to save 100 rupees every month. They make Lijjat papad, mango pickles, and handmade candles.

By doing business women earn money and don't have to depend on husband. This brings women empowerment in rural India.

question: "The rise of technocracy in Indian governance risks depoliticizing policymaking". Critically examine its role in democratic governance. (150 words)
candidate_answer:
Technology is spreading rapidly throughout the world. In India everyone has 5G internet and smartphone to use WhatsApp and Instagram. Government has introduced UPI and online ticketing for Indian Railways.

Technocrats are people who know computer programming. They should run the country because politicians don't know technology. Computers make zero mistakes so policy will become 100% perfect.

question: How does PARAKH address assessment disparities and promote holistic education? Discuss the challenges associated with its implementation. (150 words)
What is Minilateralism? Examine the role of minilateral groupings such as the Quad and the Squad in countering China's assertiveness in the Indo-Pacific region. (150 words)
candidate_answer:
Quad is an international military group formed by India, United States, China and Russia to fight pirates in Indian Ocean and protect oil tankers.

China has built big navy ships and wants to capture Taiwan and South China Sea. India should buy more fighter jets from France and America to teach lesson to enemy countries.

question: India's foreign policy is increasingly navigating a "post-Western" global order. Critically examine this trend and its strategic consequences for India's multilateral engagement. (150 words)
candidate_answer:
Western countries like England and America were very powerful earlier because they ruled many colonies. But now their economy is declining due to inflation.

India has 140 crore population and under leadership of PM Modi India is becoming Vishwaguru. India has good friendship with Russia, America and Arab countries because of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.

question: "The Speaker plays a vital role in upholding the integrity of parliamentary proceedings, but increasing politicization has raised questions about the impartiality of the office." Critically examine the role, powers and challenges faced by the Speaker in the Indian parliamentary system. (250 words)
candidate_answer:
Speaker is the leader of Lok Sabha. When MPs shout and come to the well of the house, Speaker has a big wooden hammer and shouts 'Baith jaiye, please take your seat'.

Speaker can suspend opposition MPs if they disturb proceedings of Parliament. Opposition always complains that Speaker is biased towards ruling party and does not give mike to opposition.

Speaker should be like a school principal who treats all students equally without seeing which party they belong to. Good discipline is needed so bills can be passed without noise.

question: The insertion of "Socialist" and "Secular" into the Preamble through the 42nd Amendment sparked enduring debates on constitutional morality and ideological identity. Examine the historical context and contemporary relevance of these additions. (250 words)
candidate_answer:
The words Socialist and Secular were inserted by Dr B.R. Ambedkar on 26th January 1950 when Constitution was originally written. Secular means all religions like Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Christian are brothers.

Socialism means rich people should give money to poor people so that poverty is eliminated. In 1976 Mahatma Gandhi said that Preamble is the soul of Constitution.

Today some people say these words should be removed because India is a Hindu majority country. But secularism is very good for communal harmony.

question: Discuss the statutory basis, jurisdiction, and functions of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in India. Critically analyze the challenges to its autonomy and effectiveness. (250 words)
candidate_answer:
The Indus Valley Civilization (also known as the Harappan Civilization) was one of the earliest urban civilizations in the bronze age, dating back to 2500 BCE along the banks of the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra rivers.

Key features of Indus Valley Civilization:
1. Urban Planning: Cities like Harappa and Mohenjodaro were divided into a Citadel and Lower Town with wide streets cutting at right angles in a grid system.
2. Drainage Architecture: Unique covered brick drains ran along every street with soak pits for cleaning.
3. Great Bath: A large water tank at Mohenjodaro with bitumen waterproofing used for public ritual bathing.
4. Trade & Seals: Steatite seals depicting Pashupati, Unicorn, and Bull used for long-distance maritime trade with Mesopotamia (Dilmun and Meluhha).

The decline of Harappa was caused by climate change, drying up of Saraswati river, and tectonic shifts.

question: Discuss the causes and consequences of fiscal imbalance between the Centre and the states in India. How has the introduction of GST impacted the financial autonomy of states? (250 words)
candidate_answer:
GST was introduced in 2017 by Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Centre collects all taxes like income tax, corporate tax and GST and keeps all money in Delhi.

States don't have money so they cannot pay salary to government school teachers and doctors. Centre should give 80% money to states. GST has created confusion and small shopkeepers are troubled with filling 3 returns every month.

question: "The shift from 'government' to 'governance' has created a complex network of actors, but not necessarily accountability." Critically evaluate this statement in the Indian context. (250 words)
candidate_answer:
Government is bad because government offices have red tapism and clerks ask for bribe to move files. Governance is private companies like Tata, Infosys and Reliance running the country efficiently.

Now NGOs, private hospitals and international companies are doing everything. When private companies do work there is no corruption because they want profit. But poor people have to pay high fees.

question: Despite multiple judicial pronouncements, police reforms remain elusive in India. Examine the systemic obstacles and suggest a viable roadmap. (250 words)
candidate_answer:
In India police is very corrupt and takes hafta from street vendors and truck drivers. When poor people go to police station to file FIR, police thrashes them and locks them up.

Bollywood movies like Singham and Dabangg show how brave police officers should shoot criminals directly in encounter without waiting for slow court trials.

Roadmap for police reform:
1. Increase police salary to 1 lakh per month so they stop taking bribes.
2. Give them modern AK-47 guns and bulletproof Scorpio cars.
3. Make physical fitness test mandatory every 6 months to reduce big bellies.

question: "Affirmative action has achieved representation but not transformation". Critically analyze this statement in light of reservation policies and socio-economic data. (250 words)
candidate_answer:
Reservation was introduced only for 10 years by Sardar Patel but politicians keep extending it forever to win elections. General category students score 99 marks but still don't get admission in IIT and AIIMS.

Meanwhile rich reserved students with BMW cars get seats at 40 marks. This is causing huge brain drain as talented students are leaving India and going to America and Germany. Reservation should be based only on poverty line income and not caste.

question: "Capacity building is essential for ensuring inclusive growth and effective social justice delivery." Examine the role of capacity-building initiatives in improving outcomes in education, health, and skill development in India. (250 words)
The expansion of BRICS reflects changing power dynamics in global politics. Discuss the strategic, economic, and diplomatic implications for India. (250 words)
candidate_answer:
Yoga is an ancient physical, mental and spiritual practice that originated in India over 5000 years ago during the Vedic period by Maharishi Patanjali.

On 21st June every year, United Nations celebrates International Day of Yoga across all continents. Practicing Surya Namaskar and Pranayama cures blood pressure, diabetes, anxiety, and depression.

Under the Ministry of AYUSH, Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy are getting global recognition. India should export Ayurvedic herbs like Ashwagandha and Tulsi to Western countries to generate foreign exchange revenue.

question: "The strategic embrace of Israel and continued commitment to Palestine is a paradox that defines India's West Asia policy." Critically analyze this dual diplomacy. (250 words)
candidate_answer:
Israel and Palestine have been fighting a war for thousands of years. Hamas launched missiles and kidnapped people, and Israel bombarded Gaza with fighter jets, killing many innocent children.

War is very bad for humanity. Lord Buddha and Mahatma Gandhi taught non-violence (Ahimsa). Prime Minister Modi should call Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Palestinian leaders to New Delhi and make them shake hands to end the war.
